key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can use motion time series to infer both the state and hydrodynamic coefficients of floating offshore structures by embedding the Cummins equations directly into training.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven way to identify added mass, damping, and restoring terms for offshore dynamics models when direct hydrodynamic testing is limited or costly.
method: Reformulate the Cummins equations as a first-order dynamical system.
Train a PINN on available translational and rotational motion data.
Solve the inverse problem to estimate hydrodynamic coefficients from the learned dynamics.
evidence_signal: The method was verified on free-decay cases for a sphere and a box, and it recovered state and coefficients accurately when sufficient movement data were available.
watch_item: Accuracy depends strongly on the volume and quality of motion data, so sparse or noisy measurements may reduce reliability.
paper_title: Estimating Hydrodynamic Coefficients for Floating Offshore Structures from Movement Data Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
